title: Bank statement CSV to budget: check before importing
dek: Check dates, signs, transfers and totals before categorizing a bank CSV, then add future bills so past transactions become a usable budget input.
metaDescription: Turn a bank statement CSV into reliable budget data by checking date formats, signs, duplicates, transfers and reconciliation before importing.

paragraphs: To use a bank statement CSV for a budget, keep the original download, import a copy with explicit date and amount formats, reconcile its totals and review transfers before categorizing. Then add current balances, future income and unpaid obligations. A transaction file describes a period of activity; it is not a complete forward-looking budget.

A grocery payment shown as income can make a neat chart completely wrong. So can counting both a card purchase and its later card payment as spending. Before choosing categories, establish what each column means and which accounts are included. Banks export different layouts, and some exports include pending entries rather than only posted transactions.

body.heading: Run the import in this order
items: Download through the bank's official website and record the account, date range and export settings.
Keep the original untouched and work from a copy in a restricted location.
Preview the file without enabling formulas or active content.
Identify the date format, currency, delimiter and amount or debit/credit columns.
Map transaction amounts, not the running balance, to the amount field.
Compare transaction count and inflow/outflow totals with the same bank activity period.
Resolve duplicate candidates, transfers, refunds and pending-to-posted changes.
Categorize the reconciled data and add future commitments separately.

body.heading: Invented example: four rows need four decisions
rows: Spending if the bank confirms negative means outflow
Investigate; identical text is not proof of duplication
Income after confirming source and posted status

body.heading: Check formats before trusting the preview
paragraphs: The [Microsoft import guidance](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/import-or-export-text-txt-or-csv-files) explains that opening a CSV directly uses default interpretation settings. A controlled text/CSV import gives you a chance to inspect formats. Check an unambiguous date against the bank account and preserve identifiers with leading zeros as text.

A file using 03/05 needs more evidence to establish whether that means March 5 or May 3. Amounts may use decimal commas, thousands separators, parentheses for outflows or separate debit and credit columns. Do not assume every positive value is income, particularly in credit-card exports.

If a row has shifted columns, stop and inspect the delimiter and quoting. Do not drop a malformed row simply to make the import succeed. Re-export, consult the bank's format help or record a documented correction in the working copy, preserving the original for comparison.

body.heading: Reconcile the scope before removing duplicates
paragraphs: Record the first and last included dates for every account import. Calendar months are convenient, but explicit non-overlapping ranges matter more than the name of the month. Some exporters use inclusive boundaries; check the actual rows. An overlapping file can duplicate an import even if each file is valid.

Compare totals for the same account, dates and posted/pending status. Where the bank provides matching opening and closing balances, test whether opening balance plus inflows minus outflows reconciles, while accounting for the bank's display conventions. Investigate a mismatch instead of inventing an adjustment to force agreement.

Two equal purchases on the same date may both be real. Use transaction identifiers when available and compare the official activity details. A pending authorization may later post with a different amount or description. Keep an exception list until you understand it; do not count both versions blindly.

body.heading: Avoid counting your own money twice
paragraphs: When both accounts are in scope, a transfer to savings is an outflow from one and inflow to another, not new income or consumption. Match the two sides. A card payment is also movement between your accounts if the underlying card purchases are already counted. If only one account is imported, label the transfer clearly rather than pretending missing detail is known.

Refunds should be connected to the original category where practical. Do not classify every positive row as wages. If a refund relates to an earlier month, choose and document a consistent reporting approach so comparisons remain understandable.

CSV files contain sensitive transaction details. Review the destination's privacy and retention terms before uploading, share the minimum needed, and remove unnecessary copies securely. A manual download avoids supplying a bank login for that transfer, but does not make the data harmless. For the next planning layer, use a [monthly bills list](/guides/monthly-bills-list).

items.q: Can I build a budget from a CSV alone?
items.a: It can show historical spending and income for the exported scope, but not every future obligation or current available balance. Add upcoming bills, essential spending and confirmed incoming money. Also check for accounts, cash transactions or annual expenses outside the file before calling the budget complete.

items.q: Should I delete matching transactions automatically?
items.a: No. Matching date, description and amount make a useful review flag, not proof that a row is duplicated. Two genuine purchases can match. Compare transaction identifiers, import ranges and bank activity before excluding a row, and keep a record of what was excluded and why.

items.q: Why did my dates change in the spreadsheet?
items.a: The spreadsheet may have interpreted them using its default locale or date format. Re-import the original copy with explicit column settings and compare unambiguous entries with the bank. Do not repair dates by guessing from a chart or by changing display format after an incorrect conversion.

research.intent: Convert exported transactions into checked historical budget data without confusing them with a full forecast.
sourceChecks: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/import-or-export-text-txt-or-csv-files - opened official import documentation and checked format warnings.
limitations: No bank-specific export format or importer feature assumed.
CSV formula-safety instructions are precautionary; no malicious sample supplied.
Historical files may omit accounts, pending entries or future bills.
